about.description: What it does, in a sentence or two.

hours.description: Its days and hours, as the agent may say them.

timezone.description: The business's IANA time zone (for example America/New_York): what "today" means for its calendar. Default: UTC.

open.description: The business's opening hours, as the line can read them (in the business's time zone). With them the line tells the model whether the business is open now, and until when or when it next opens, and lines.greetingAfterHours is said when a call starts while it is closed. `hours` stays the text the agent may say; this is what the line itself works from.

weekly.description: Day names (mon ... sun) or ranges of them (mon-fri) to lists of HH:MM-HH:MM ranges in 24-hour time; a range whose end is before its start runs overnight, and 24:00 ends one at midnight.

closed.description: Dates (YYYY-MM-DD) the business is closed all day.

line.description: The business's reason for the line, said to a caller who is not giving what it asks for (for example "This line is how we price repairs and set up drop-offs while we are busy in the shop"). Used only with journeys.

services.description: What the business does, with a price range where it has one.

per.description: What the price is for (a visit, a unit).

en.description: What the agent says alongside any price (for example that the final price is confirmed once the work is seen), in English.

priceCaveat.description: What the agent says alongside any price (for example that the final price is confirmed once the work is seen), per language.

notOffered.description: What the business does not do.

facts.description: Anything else the agent may say, one fact each.

questions.description: The questions callers ask and the business's answers: what to bring, how long things take, when someone calls back, what it costs to cancel. Where the business has not answered a question, the agent has nothing to go on; the simulated callers' judge lists such answers as gaps for the owner to fill in here.

q.description: A question callers ask, in their words.

a.description: The business's answer, as the agent may say it.

opener.description: acknowledge: each reply begins with a brief, natural acknowledgement that commits the business to nothing ("Got it."), varied, and left out where it would sound odd, so the caller hears a whole first sentence almost at once. Absent: no opener is asked for.

voices.description: The voice to use per carrier.

en.description: The greeting, in English.

chat.description: The greeting in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The greeting in the web chat, in English.
The closing line, in English.

chat.description: The closing line in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The closing line in the web chat, in English.
The short line said when the agent did not catch something, in English.

chat.description: The short line said when the agent did not catch something in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The short line said when the agent did not catch something in the web chat, in English.

recovery.description: The short line said when the agent did not catch something, per language.

en.description: The line said when the call goes to a person, in English.

chat.description: The line said when the call goes to a person in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The line said when the call goes to a person in the web chat, in English.

handoff.description: The line said when the call goes to a person, per language.

en.description: The line said when the caller did not confirm a read-back, in English.

chat.description: The line said when the caller did not confirm a read-back in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The line said when the caller did not confirm a read-back in the web chat, in English.

notConfirmed.description: The line said when the caller did not confirm a read-back, per language.

en.description: The line said when an action the caller confirmed has run but the reply after it failed, so the caller still hears it was done, in English.

chat.description: The line said when an action the caller confirmed has run but the reply after it failed, so the caller still hears it was done in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The line said when an action the caller confirmed has run but the reply after it failed, so the caller still hears it was done in the web chat, in English.

done.description: The line said when an action the caller confirmed has run but the reply after it failed, so the caller still hears it was done, per language.

en.description: The line said, and the call ended, on the third turn in a row the line could not follow (required when there are journeys), in English.

chat.description: The line said, and the call ended, on the third turn in a row the line could not follow (required when there are journeys) in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The line said, and the call ended, on the third turn in a row the line could not follow (required when there are journeys) in the web chat, in English.

unclear.description: The line said, and the call ended, on the third turn in a row the line could not follow (required when there are journeys), per language.

en.description: The greeting said instead of the greeting (and of a journey's) when a call starts while the business is closed by business.open (required to have business.open), in English.

chat.description: The greeting said instead of the greeting (and of a journey's) when a call starts while the business is closed by business.open (required to have business.open) in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The greeting said instead of the greeting (and of a journey's) when a call starts while the business is closed by business.open (required to have business.open) in the web chat, in English.

greetingAfterHours.description: The greeting said instead of the greeting (and of a journey's) when a call starts while the business is closed by business.open (required to have business.open), per language.

default.en: Let me have someone follow up on that.

en.description: The line said when the model is still looking things up after its last round of a turn (where nothing the caller confirmed has just run), in English.

chat.description: The line said when the model is still looking things up after its last round of a turn (where nothing the caller confirmed has just run) in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: The line said when the model is still looking things up after its last round of a turn (where nothing the caller confirmed has just run) in the web chat, in English.

stuck.description: The line said when the model is still looking things up after its last round of a turn (where nothing the caller confirmed has just run), per language.

lines.description: The lines said word for word.

default.description: The model, as <provider>:<model> (anthropic, inception, openrouter or meta). Claude models go through anthropic only. An OpenRouter model may name the hosts it is asked on after @ (openrouter:openai/gpt-oss-120b@groq), with no fallback to others; OpenRouter is always asked for hosts that collect no data.

timeoutMs.description: How long a model reply may take before the turn falls back.

maxTokens.description: The most tokens a reply may use (a model's reasoning counts toward it). A reply cut off at it is a failed turn, never spoken as it was cut.

effort.description: How hard the model reasons: minimal, low, medium or high, sent in each provider's own form (Inception's reasoning_effort, where minimal is its instant; Meta's reasoning_effort; OpenRouter's reasoning.effort; Anthropic's output_config.effort, where minimal is low). Default: the provider's own.

model.description: The model that leads the conversation.

limits.description: When to stop trying and offer a person.

failuresPerCall.description: Failed turns in a call before it goes to a person.

refusalsPerAction.description: Refusals of the same action before the agent offers a person.

checks.description: Checks the runtime makes of what the agent model says.

claims.description: The check after speaking (docs/designs/2026-11-11-claims-check.md): each reply of the agent model read by the decision model once it is said.

mode.description: correct: the decision model reads each reply of the agent model once it has been said; a reply read as contradicted by the business information or the call's actions, or as saying something was done that was not, goes back to the model with a note, and its correction is said after it; a gap (a commitment the business information does not address) is recorded. record: each reply is read and its readings recorded, nothing said. off: no reply is read. Default: off (measured, it did not tell wrong replies from right ones; docs/designs/2026-11-11-claims-check.md).

correctAt.description: The bar a reading of contradicted or of not done must reach for the reply to be corrected (with mode correct) and recorded as such. A number over 0 and at most 1. Default: 0.7.

gapAt.description: The bar a reading of a gap must reach for it to be recorded as one. A number over 0 and at most 1. Default: 0.7.

sources.description: Where the calendar and the caller accounts come from.

kind.description: fake: the days and windows below, for a demo. google: reserved for a later release.

days.description: The days the business is open to book, as dates.

windows.description: The windows of a day a visit may be booked into, each with its capacity.

label.description: How it is said to a caller (for example "9 to 12").

until.description: The last time a car may be dropped off in it, as 24-hour "HH:MM" in the business's time zone. Today's window is not offered or bookable after it; a later day's is unchanged. Absent, the window is offered all day.

accounts.description: Caller accounts, recognised by the number they call from.

numbers.description: The numbers it calls from: E.164, or env.<NAME>. A variable that is not set is left out.

items.description: A caller account, recognised by the numbers it calls from.

actions.description: Every action the agent may call, by name.

about.description: What the action does and when to use it, for the model.

kind.description: lookup: reads and returns a result. change: does something, and so is read back and confirmed by the caller first.

params.description: The parameters the call carries, by name.

type.description: How the value is checked: date (a real date), slot (one the named lookup returned on this call), choice (one of the options), number, text, phone (a phone number).

about.description: What the value is, in plain words, for the model.

options.description: For a choice: the values it may take.

from.description: For a slot: the lookup action whose results the value must come from.

optional.description: The model may leave the value out. Default: the value is required.

max.description: For a text: the most characters it may have (it is said in the read-back as it was given). Default: 120.

en.description: The read-back said before a change runs, with each parameter as a {placeholder} named as the parameter, an optional one in a part in square brackets said only when it has a value ("[, {details}]"); required for a change, in English.

readBack.description: The read-back said before a change runs, with each parameter as a {placeholder} named as the parameter, an optional one in a part in square brackets said only when it has a value ("[, {details}]"); required for a change, per language.

then.description: Actions that run after the confirmed yes with no read-back of their own, each still through the gate. Only on a change.

rules.description: The gate's rules for this action, in the same shape as policy.yaml's.

anyOf.description: A rule with no parameters: identity (the caller's identity level is at least the action's) or attempts (the identity check has failed fewer times than identity.yaml's attempts).

param.description: The action's param that is the subject's own id (for example accountId).

record.description: The action's param that is a record id the gate resolves to its owner (for example recordId).

scope.description: scope: the subject the action acts on must be one the caller may see. Exactly one of "param" (the param is the subject's own id) or "record" (the param is a record id, resolved to its owner).

anyOf.description: The scope rule with its parameters, for example "scope: { param: accountId }".

reason.description: The reason a "person" role hands the call over for (its handoff line is handoff_<reason>). Default "role-person".

role.description: role: what each role may do with the action: allow, refuse, or person (a person takes the call). A role not listed is refused, and so is a party who acts for subjects with no role; one of the app's subjects passes. The roles are those identity.yaml declares under principals.

anyOf.description: The role rule with its parameters, for example "role: { viewer: refuse, clerk: person }".

confirmed.description: confirmed: the action sends exactly these fields, and the caller confirmed exactly these values at the read-back, in the order the hash is taken over.

anyOf.description: The confirmed rule with its parameters, for example "confirmed: [accountId, note]".

fields.description: fields: the only fields the action may send on (to a downstream service). An empty list sends none.

anyOf.description: The fields rule with its parameters, for example "fields: [note, date]".

field.description: The action's param that holds the date (yyyy-mm-dd). A value that is not a date BLOCKs.

notBefore.description: The earliest date the value may be, inclusive: "today", today+N or today-N (N days from today, 1 to 3660), a date, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

notAfter.description: The latest date the value may be, inclusive: "today", today+N or today-N (N days from today, 1 to 3660), a date, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

within.description: A reference to a lookup that gives a window, { start, end } (end null: open-ended), the value must be inside, ends inclusive. A lookup that gives null has no window: the value is outside it.

unscoped.description: true: the lookups this rule's bounds call are not about the caller's own record (a price list, a calendar), so their params need no scope rule before this one. Without it, every param a reference reads must be held to the caller's own records by a scope rule earlier in the action.

reasons.description: The reason the gate gives for each way the rule fails, for the app's refusal lines and handoffs.

invalid.description: The reason a value that is not a date is refused for. Default "not-a-date".

outOfRange.description: The reason a date before notBefore or after notAfter fails for. Default "date-range".

outsideWindow.description: The reason a date outside the window fails for. Default "date-window".

verdicts.description: The verdict for a date out of its bounds or outside its window. A value that is not a date, and a bound that cannot be found, always BLOCK.

outOfRange.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a date out of its bounds.

outsideWindow.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a date outside the window.

dateInRange.description: dateInRange: the action's date param is a date within its bounds, each inclusive. At least one of notBefore, notAfter, within.

anyOf.description: The dateInRange rule with its parameters, for example "dateInRange: { field: returnDate, notAfter: today }".

field.description: The action's param that holds the number: digits, an optional leading minus and an optional point with digits; no units, separators or spaces. Anything else BLOCKs.

min.description: The smallest the number may be, inclusive: a number, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

max.description: The largest the number may be, inclusive: a number, or a reference to a lookup that gives one (for example orderTotal(orderId), or order(orderId).total).

unscoped.description: true: the lookups this rule's bounds call are not about the caller's own record (a price list, a calendar), so their params need no scope rule before this one. Without it, every param a reference reads must be held to the caller's own records by a scope rule earlier in the action.

reasons.description: The reason the gate gives for each way the rule fails.

invalid.description: The reason a value that is not a number is refused for. Default "not-a-number".

outOfRange.description: The reason a number below min or above max fails for. Default "limit".

verdicts.description: The verdict for a number outside its limits. A value that is not a number, and a bound that cannot be found, always BLOCK.

outOfRange.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a number outside its limits.

limit.description: limit: the action's number param is within its limits, each inclusive. At least one of min, max.

anyOf.description: The limit rule with its parameters, for example "limit: { field: amount, max: orderTotal(orderId) }".

field.description: The action's param that holds the value (for a check, one of the slots its `with` sends). A value that is missing or empty BLOCKs, reason "value-missing".

values.description: The values the param must be one of, each as the slot holds it (a choice slot's option ids), matched exactly.

reason.description: The reason a value not listed fails for, for a form check's `on:`, the app's refusal lines and handoffs. Default "not-one-of".

verdict.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a value not listed. A missing value always BLOCKs.

oneOf.description: oneOf: the action's param is one of the values listed.

anyOf.description: The oneOf rule with its parameters, for example "oneOf: { field: town, values: [millbrook, ashford] }".

field.description: The action's param that holds the value (for a check, one of the slots its `with` sends). A value that is missing or empty BLOCKs, reason "value-missing".

values.description: The values the param must not be, each as the slot holds it (a choice slot's option ids), matched exactly.

reason.description: The reason a value listed fails for, for a form check's `on:`, the app's refusal lines and handoffs. Default "one-of".

verdict.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a value listed. A missing value always BLOCKs.

noneOf.description: noneOf: the action's param is none of the values listed.

anyOf.description: The noneOf rule with its parameters, for example "noneOf: { field: howUrgent, values: [emergency], verdict: NEEDS_HUMAN }".

field.description: The action's param that holds the number (for a text, the slot a text offer filled: it is compared as that slot holds the caller's number). A value that is missing or empty BLOCKs, reason "value-missing".

else.description: What a number that is not the caller's gets: "refuse" (default), BLOCK "not-caller-number" (or "no-caller-number" when the call kept none), or "confirmed": it passes when the caller heard the call's values read back at the summary and said yes, which needs the field in the action's confirmed rule.

withheld.description: What the caller's own number gets when they withheld it (*67) and the carrier sent it anyway: "allow" (default), it passes as any caller's number; "refuse", BLOCK "caller-number-withheld" (a number confirmed at the summary, with else: confirmed, still passes). Honouring the caller's privacy is the app's decision; app.yaml's callerNumber.withheld: ignore does it for every feature at once.

callerNumber.description: callerNumber: the action's param is the number the caller is calling from, or with else: confirmed one they confirmed at the summary. Caller ID is a hint, never identity: the rule says where a call may send something, never whose record it reads.

anyOf.description: The callerNumber rule with its parameters, for example "callerNumber: { field: textTo }".

custom.description: custom: one of the app's own rules, by the id its code registers it under (code.customRules).

anyOf.description: The custom rule with its parameters, for example "custom: <the rule's id in code.customRules>".

items.description: One rule: a bare name (identity, attempts) or a map of one rule to its parameters (scope, role, confirmed, fields, dateInRange, limit, oneOf, noneOf, callerNumber, custom).

audit.description: How each param that needs it is recorded: last4, mask, length, secret or keep. Default: mask.

additionalProperties.description: One action the agent may call.

root.description: The line when no journey is active.

instructions.description: How the line answers when no journey is active: the business's own guidance, never a script.

actions.description: The actions offered at the root: lookups only. Default: none.

routing.description: How each caller turn is routed to a journey.

switchAt.description: The bar the decision model's reading must reach for the line to move to another journey. A number over 0 and at most 1. Default: 0.6.

startAt.description: The bar the decision model's reading must reach for a journey to start from the root; below it the turn is unclear. At least switchAt. The default, 0.7, is the value measured on labelled caller turns (docs/designs/eval/2026-11-journeys.md). A number over 0 and at most 1. Default: 0.7.

timeoutMs.description: How long the decision model may take to read a turn before the turn goes on with the active journey (or the root). Default: 400.

journeys.description: The tasks the line can take on, by id. Absent: one conversation with every action, as before.

when.description: The trigger, in plain words: what the caller wants. It is what the decision model reads, and what the root model is told the line can help with. Say what the caller wants, never who they are.

goal.description: What the journey achieves, in one sentence.

instructions.description: What to collect, what to check first, what not to mention. Goals and limits, never wording.

facts.description: This journey's own facts, added to the base's for this journey only. A journey cannot remove or override a base fact.

questions.description: This journey's own questions callers ask, with the business's answers, added to the base's for this journey only.

q.description: A question callers ask, in their words.

a.description: The business's answer, as the agent may say it.

actions.description: The actions it may use, named from the top-level actions. Each action is defined once and may be named by several journeys.

for.description: Which callers the journey is open to, by a fact of the call. A journey closed to the caller is never one of the decision model's options. Absent: open to every caller.

account.description: recognised: open only where the number calling is on an account. none: open only where it is on none.

en.description: What the line says first where this journey starts the call (it has `start`), instead of lines.greeting, in English.

chat.description: What the line says first where this journey starts the call (it has `start`), instead of lines.greeting in the web chat, per language, where it is worded differently from the call (for example "Thanks for messaging" for "Thanks for calling"). Absent: the chat says the same words as the call.

en.description: What the line says first where this journey starts the call (it has `start`), instead of lines.greeting in the web chat, in English.

greeting.description: What the line says first where this journey starts the call (it has `start`), instead of lines.greeting, per language.

start.description: A fact of the call that starts the journey before the caller speaks. At most one journey says it.

account.description: Start where the number calling is on an account.

completes.description: The change actions whose confirmed run ends the journey. Default: all the change actions it names that are not follow-ons.

after.description: What the line helps with once the journey is done, in one sentence. Default: "<goal>: done on this call. Answer the caller's questions about it."

additionalProperties.description: One journey: a task the line can take on, with its own instructions, facts and actions.

transfer.description: Where a call goes when it is handed to a person.

number.description: The number to hand a call to: E.164, or env.<NAME>.
